posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked: I propose that Chrono-Ranger gets the Talisman, both because he gets first shot (heheh) at using it, and because he gets extra power usages out of The Ultimate Target, while still able to deal damage with card plays.  It might eventually be wise to give it to Bunker so he can shrug off the damage she deals when she doesn't have it, but that damage targets any highest-HP hero rather than necessarily the one who has the Talisman, and Bunker for one is almost unquestionably never going to have a spare Power to use the Talisman on any decks, while CR could potentially use it on two or more decks each round.  (Is there any way to make Kismet deal damage on hero turns?)

posts.name: dpt
posts.cooked:
Kismet deals damage to a hero with Weak Heart. On Two Left Feet, the hero damages themself; that would be a good one to give Mr. Fixer, in case Jack Handle comes out.

 

It's worth thinking about the interaction of the Talisman with the powers of Dark Visionary and Omnitron-X. The Talisman is weak deck-stacking, but I could follow it up with discarding key cards. And Omnitron-X can Timeshift into play a key card.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked: Yeah, the Talisman can do some interesting stuff.  It's a pity that Kizzy is so violent about losing it.  I think she's the one hero where I would prefer playing on Normal rather than Advanced,  not because the latter is too hard (though it certainly is, particularly with H=5) or unnecessarily prolonged (Dawn), but simply because there's more fun to be had when she's not trying as hard to kill you.  This contrasts nicely with our last episode, where Spite got to be so invincible that there was no point even trying to hurt him, so we were forced into a new "give him what he wants" playstyle.  That was really neat.
